params.body:
# Why

The first `/stocklist` Livewire request after a deploy hung on staging for over thirty seconds and
PHP-FPM killed the worker at 37 s. The acceptance test runs on staging today, so a first visitor
who gets a dead page is the whole problem.

# The slowlog stack

```
DemoMediaDisk::zoek() (app/Support/DemoMediaDisk.php:66)
  -> Cache::remember closure (line 79)
    -> FilesystemAdapter::exists()
      -> League\Flysystem\Filesystem::has()
        -> AwsS3V3Adapter::directoryExists()
          -> AWS SDK execute -> Guzzle -> curl_multi_select (waiting)
```

Three things stack up in that frame.

1. `zoek()` wants to know whether one FILE exists under `demo/`, but it asked
   `Storage::exists()`, and Laravel's `exists()` is `fileExists() || directoryExists()`. On a miss
   that is a HEAD **plus** a ListObjectsV2 against Hetzner object storage.
2. It asked that once per photo path, serially, while the page rendered. A stocklist page is 20
   cards, each with a primary photo and up to eight carousel photos, so up to 180 distinct paths.
   Every photo the backfill has not reached yet (`media_version` is null, and the backfill is
   capped at vehicle folder 20710) misses the derived-path shortcut and gets its own probe.
3. Nothing bounded the wait. The S3 disks had no `connect_timeout` and no `timeout`, so the SDK
   waits as long as the bucket takes, and the SDK's three retries multiply that.

`DemoMediaDisk` only wraps the disks outside production (`Outbound::seal()`), so this is a
staging and demo fault only.

# What changed

**The cheapest question** (`app/Support/DemoMediaDisk.php`). The probe is now `fileExists()` - one
HEAD - and never the combined `exists()` that also lists a directory. `delete()` uses the same
file-only probe. A disk that does not know `fileExists()` keeps the old call rather than breaking.

**Ask it at most once per folder.** The demo writes into a handful of folders at most, so one
shallow listing of `demo/` (one ListObjectsV2 with a delimiter, which returns folder names and not
the objects inside them, so the big `demo/_afgeleid` tree costs nothing) says which folders the
demo ever touched. A path in a folder that is not on that list cannot be in the demo and is
answered without any call. The list is cached, and every write forgets it before and after the
write, so a folder the demo has just created is seen immediately. Answers are also memoised per
request, because a card grid asks for the same folder over and over.

**Fail fast instead of hanging** (`config/filesystems.php`). The four S3 disks get
`connect_timeout` 2 s, `timeout` 15 s and one retry instead of three (`AWS_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`,
`AWS_TIMEOUT`, `AWS_RETRIES` override them). The read timeout is deliberately generous, because it
also covers uploading a photo of a few megabytes; the sharp bound for the render path lives in
`DemoMediaDisk` itself, which gives all its probes together a 3 s budget per request and answers
"not in the demo" for the rest once that is spent. A probe that throws is treated as "not found",
which serves the real file - exactly what the environment showed before anyone uploaded anything -
and it is remembered for ten seconds only, so a bucket that comes back is picked up at once. A
decided answer keeps the five-minute cache.

`App\Support\S3Presigner` needed nothing: it computes a SigV4 signature with four HMACs and never
touches the network, and it already routes through `DemoMediaDisk::resolve()`. `resolve()`'s
shortcut for derived paths is unchanged.

# Cost before and after

A first cold `/stocklist` render, 20 cards, up to 180 distinct photo paths, no warm cache:

| | S3 calls |
| --- | --- |
| Before | up to 2 per path that is not a derived size: one HEAD plus one ListObjectsV2, serially. Up to about 360, unbounded in time, which is the 37 s. |
| After | 1 ListObjectsV2 for the folder list, plus one HEAD for each path that lies in a folder the demo really wrote into. On a demo that has uploaded nothing that is exactly **1**; after a demo has uploaded into three vehicle folders it is 1 plus at most the photos of those three cards. |
| Second render (cache warm) | 0, as before. |

Worst case is now bounded twice over: by the disk timeouts, and by the 3 s probe budget per
request.

# Production unaffected

`DemoMediaDisk` is installed only by `Outbound::seal()`, which never runs in production, so none of
the lookup code above exists there. The rule that the demo never writes or deletes outside `demo/`
is untouched, and its tests still pin it. The only production-visible change is the S3 timeouts,
which replace "wait forever" with "give up after 2 s connecting or 15 s reading, once"; they are
env-overridable.

# Checked

`php artisan test --filter='DemoMedia|VehicleImage|Stocklist|SmokeTest|Warm'` - 173 tests, 330
assertions, green. Full suite: 526 tests, one failure that is an artifact of running in a git
worktree (`BuildStampTest` reads the commit stamp from the checkout).

`tests/Feature/DemoMediaTest.php` gained six cases: the probe calls `fileExists` and never `exists`
or `directoryExists`; ten paths outside any demo folder cost one listing and zero probes; a bucket
that throws on every call answers "not in the demo" instead of throwing; a failed probe is
remembered as a short negative and a failed listing is not remembered at all; a file the demo wrote
is still found, including in a folder that did not exist before the write; and a derived size is
still never looked up.
params.title: Staging: the demo disk no longer lists the bucket per photo
